Components inside the long press trigger group can be triggered by a long press. The long press events and order can be customized. To add a component, drag it onto the long press trigger group.

"Terminate Mode decides when a started action should stop.
No termination: The active action will be terminated when you release the key.
Example: Press the key → Touch A starts pressing the screen. Keep holding → Touch B starts and A keeps touching. Release the key → The current two touch actions are released at the same time.
This is useful when the action should stay active only while you are holding the key.
Terminate previous: Only one action can stay active at the same time. When a new action starts, the previous action will be terminated automatically.
Example: Press the key → Touch A starts pressing the screen. Keep holding → Touch B starts, and Touch A is released. Keep holding longer → Touch C starts, and Touch B is released.
This is useful when each hold level should replace the previous action."
Drag other components above this component to add other components to long press group

A long-press trigger group with the same key already exists. Please add the new key you want to trigger by long press to that same-key long-press trigger group; otherwise, the long-press trigger keys will not be linked together.

"Trigger Mode decides how the app handles different hold times for the same key.
Sequential: Actions are triggered one after another while you keep holding the key.
Example: Press the key → Action A triggers. Keep holding → Action B triggers. Keep holding longer → Action C triggers.
This is useful when one long press should run several actions in order.
Duration match: Only one action will trigger. The app waits until you release the key, then checks how long you held it.
Example: Quick release → Action A triggers. Medium hold → Action B triggers. Long hold → Action C triggers.
This is useful when different hold lengths should do different actions."

"By default, the game camera control touch point can move anywhere on the screen.
Enable this option if you want to restrict it to a specific area. Once enabled, the game camera control touch point will stay inside the area you set and will not move outside it. After this option is enabled, go to keymap editor and drag to resize the area"

"Edge Release Only
This option controls when the view-control touch point is released.
By default, the app periodically releases the view-control touch point after the time set in Non-edge Release Time Interval. This helps prevent possible game camera issues when you are not moving the mouse.
When this option is enabled, the view-control touch point will not be released periodically. It will only be released and placed again when it reaches the edge of the control area."

"Reset View
This works the same as pressing the Display hotkey twice. When you press the Reset View hotkey, the app resets the view-control touch point back to its initial position.
This is useful if your mouse can no longer control the game camera or view correctly. When this happens, press the Reset View hotkey to restore normal view control."

This slider allows you to set the duration of a single tap - that is, the time interval between a simulated finger down and up. For example, if it is set to 100, it will simulate a finger up after 100 milliseconds after finger down for each click. Setting below 100 is not recommended, because it will increase the chance of being banned.

This slider allows you to set the interval between each tap. For example, if it is set to 100, there will be a delay of 100 milliseconds after each tap before the next tap is triggered. Setting below 100 is not recommended, because it will increase the chance of being banned

When the associated viewpoint switch is on, pressing the key that this button is bound to and moving the mouse will control the viewpoint starting from this button position (e.g. small eyes in FPS). If you want to control the small eyes, you can turn this switch on by moving the key and aligning it with the small eyes.
When this switch is on, you can switch mouse display state when pressing the hotkey.

"Toggle Lock Trigger Mode: 1. pressing the key to toggle, pressing the bound key to toggle the mouse pointer lock 2. pressing the key to toggle, lifting the bound key to toggle the mouse pointer lock 3. pressing the lift to toggle, pressing and lifting the bound key will toggle the pointer locked/unlocked state once each."

When this switch is turned on, pressing the bound button while the rocker is released will reactivate it. If you experience the joystick not moving after getting on or off, turn this switch on. And set the delay to slightly greater than your average network delay.

When this switch is turned on, the virtual finger that simulates the control of the viewpoint will be lifted and re-pressed when the bound button is pressed at the same time. If you encounter a situation where the viewpoint does not move after getting in and out of the car, turn this switch on. And set the delay to slightly greater than your average network delay.

"Continuous Long Press: Triggers a press when you press the keypad, triggers a lift when you release the keypad Single Tap Triggers a tap when you press the keypad Quick Tap: Tap is triggered when keypad is pressed and canceled when keypad is released Press to lift: a single tap is triggered when the keyboard is pressed and released Long press trigger: Android version to come!"

"Press: Touch the screen when you press the binding key. Stop touching screen when you release the binding key. Tap: Tap the screen once after you press the key Crazy tap: Tap the screen according to the tap duration and interval until you release the binding key Down/up tap: Tap the screen both after you press and release the binding key Up trigger: Tap the screen when you release the binding key"
